node.method_name: Invoice-bearing flows should clear in a reasonable time.

guidance.expectation: Invoices are cleared within the agreed days after the invoice (30 days, tolerance to 90 in the paper's norm; the real payment terms of the vendor once they are a case attribute).
guidance.meaning_when_missed: The invoice waited longer than the target before payment, because of a block, a payment-run calendar, long terms or a dispute.
guidance.why_it_matters: Lost discounts, vendor escalations and delivery stops when paid late; working capital paid out early when the terms are longer than the target.
guidance.how_detected: A time rule from the first invoice evidence to the clearing on invoice-bearing items, scored between met at 30 days and fully missed at 90. In BPIC 2019 the median is 63.6 days and 88.9 % of cleared items exceed 30 days, so without payment terms this rule is a lateness meter rather than a pass-fail rule; the baseline scores open invoices by their age.

guidance.how_detected: A threshold rule on the number of distinct named users in the item's events.

guidance.expectation: Receipts, invoices, block releases and payments follow each other within the agreed number of days.
guidance.meaning_when_missed: Items age between two steps; invoices wait for a receipt or a release, released invoices wait for a payment run, and vendors wait for their money.
guidance.why_it_matters: Lost early-payment discounts, vendor escalations and delivery stops, working capital tied up or paid out too early, and a backlog that accounts payable works through by hand.
guidance.how_detected: Time-between-steps rules with a target and a tolerance: receipt to invoice in GR-based flows (target 10 days, tolerance to 30 in the paper's norm), invoice to payment (30 days, tolerance to 90), receipt to block release and release to payment in invoice-first flows (2 and 5 days). Each item scores between met and fully missed according to how far beyond the target it is.

usual_reasons.check: median invoice-to-payment days per vendor; vendors with medians near 60 or 90 days follow terms, not a delay

guidance.expectation: Items pass from order to payment with as few manual touches, hand-offs and events as the flow needs.
guidance.meaning_when_missed: People had to intervene several times on the item, several people touched it, or the item collected a long chain of events.
guidance.why_it_matters: Effort in purchasing and accounts payable, waiting time at each hand-off, and errors introduced by manual work; the touchless rate is the lever for automation.
guidance.how_detected: Threshold rules on derived counts: manual touches by named users (more than 4, saturating at 10), distinct human users (more than 2), total events (more than 10) and the manual share of events (above half); batch users are excluded by name.

usual_reasons.text: Exceptions (changes, blocks, cancellations) each add manual steps
usual_reasons.check: which activities carry the manual touches, by constraint and activity

usual_reasons.text: Header events copied onto every item inflate the counts
usual_reasons.check: replication diagnostics before reading touch counts; type header events away and compare

usual_reasons.text: No electronic vendor integration, so confirmations and invoices are keyed in
usual_reasons.check: ask purchasing which vendors send EDI confirmations and e-invoices

usual_reasons.text: Batch users not recognised as such and counted as manual
usual_reasons.check: user names of the most frequent touches; batch or system users in the resource column

usual_actions.text: Touchless targets per spend area with a monthly review
EDI confirmations and e-invoicing with the largest vendors
Exception reduction upstream (price and quantity aligned before ordering)
Error-proofing in the buying front end (mandatory fields, catalogue defaults)
